page: The Vultr voc-s-8c-64gb-1280s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server featuring an AMD EPYC processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It delivers 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Local storage consists of a bundled 1280 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate strong single-core CPU capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU performance placing in the top 25% tier. Multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU scores fall within the average range. Memory performance is a notable highlight, with the PassMark memory score ranking in the top 25%, though uncached memory read and write bandwidth tests remain in the middle tier. Cryptographic operations are aided by hardware-accelerated AES and SHA_NI instruction sets.

This hardware configuration is highly suited for memory-intensive workloads, database operations, and caching layers such as Redis, where it achieves average performance tiers. The 1:8 vCPU-to-RAM ratio combined with a substantial 1280 GB NVMe SSD offers a cost-efficient profile for resource-dense environments that require significant memory and fast local storage without the overhead of dedicated GPU accelerators. It is less suited for heavy LLM prompt processing, where benchmarks show weaker relative performance.
